headline: Chezka Centeno Finishes Runner-Up at Women's World 10-Ball Championship
deck: Belarusian Margarita Fefilova Styer defeated defending champion Chezka Centeno in a five-set final in Rome to claim the women's world 10-ball title.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Filipina cueist Chezka Centeno finished runner-up at the 2026 WPA Women's 10-Ball World Championship in Rome after Margarita Fefilova Styer won their five-set final, 3-2.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: Fefilova Styer took the first three sets, 4-1, 4-0 and 4-0. Centeno answered by winning the next two, 4-1 and 4-0, before Fefilova Styer secured the deciding set, 4-0.
The Women's 10-Ball World Championship ran from July 31 to August 6 at Piazza di Spagna in Rome and carried a total prize fund of $200,000, according to the World Pool Association.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: Centeno entered the final as the defending champion after winning the women's world 10-ball title in 2025. Her Rome result followed her women's world 8-ball championship victory in July 2026.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The bulletin's links did not lead to complete articles, and its claims about post-tournament commendations and incentives were not independently documented in the sources available at publication time. Those details are not included here.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Centeno's second-place finish keeps a Filipina athlete among the leading competitors in women's international pool and extends a run that includes world titles in both 8-ball and 10-ball.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: Official federation and player channels are expected to carry details of Centeno's next international event.
